note: Second sentence is a verbless fragment (“In a way that suits my temperament…”), garbling “in some sort it jumps with my humour”.
Garbled pun: colted means tricked, but target says he is not tricked out of a horse, which contradicts the situation.
Leftover archaism “Anon” in Hal’s plan; elsewhere rendered “Coming,” which the joke depends on.
Wrong referent: the original’s parenthesis calls Titan (the sun) pitiful-hearted, not the butter.
Garbled phrasing “the four poor of us.”
Pun lost: “points” were also the laces holding up hose; with “sword points” in the line before, Poins’s joke no longer makes sense.
Wrong agent: Lancaster speaks of Hotspur by that name, he does not hear it.
Wrong meaning: the river cuts into Mortimer's land just as much; it does not give him an advantage.
Dangling participle: “being swallowed up by men’s eyes” wrongly attaches to “they” (the people), garbling who is swallowed.
Sentence fragment (“Yes, even the smallest honor… or I’ll tear…”) breaks the either/or logic of the threat.
“swore little” means seldom swore; “I swore a little” shifts the meaning and weakens the joke pattern.
Inserted a stage direction “[To Douglas.]” mid-paragraph that is not in the original.
Reversed meaning: “’Tis insensible? Yea, to the dead” means the dead cannot sense it; “Yes, by the dead” says the dead can.
